data.description:
## Symptom
An autonomous agent orchestrating rebar was KILLED mid-close by its harness: `Agent stalled: no progress for 600s (stream watchdog did not recover)`. It died immediately after reporting it was auditing residual gaps for an epic close — i.e. at the point it would have invoked a close / `verify-completion` / `review-plan` gate. All nine of its code changes had already landed; the epic and one story were left stranded `in_progress` with every descendant closed, requiring a separate session to finish the two transitions.

## Mechanism
rebar's LLM gate operations (`transition ... closed` with the completion-verification gate enabled, `review-plan`, `verify-completion`) run a single long model call and emit NOTHING to stdout/stderr between start and final verdict. Measured in this session:

- `rebar transition <story> in_progress closed` — exceeded a 600s foreground timeout, then ran to completion in the background. Total output before the final `transitioned ...` line: three unrelated `enrich_drain` warnings and one build-drift advisory. No progress indication for the duration.
- `rebar review-plan <epic>` — same shape, still producing no output minutes in.

Any supervisor that treats "no output" as "no progress" therefore cannot distinguish a healthy 10-minute gate call from a hung process, and will kill a correct run. This is not specific to one harness: a 600s silence budget is an ordinary default.

## Why this is rebar's problem, not only the supervisor's
The gates are the sanctioned, documented path for claiming and closing work (AGENTS.md requires them), and closing is the LAST step of a long autonomous run — so the failure lands where the most state is at risk and the most work has already been invested. An operation that routinely runs longer than common watchdog budgets while emitting nothing is hostile to the automation rebar is explicitly designed for.

## Suggested remedies (any one would break the failure)
1. Emit periodic progress to stderr during a long gate call — even a heartbeat naming the phase (`prompt built`, `model call issued`, `awaiting verdict`, elapsed seconds).
2. Stream or chunk the model interaction so output appears incrementally.
3. Document the expected wall-clock range for each gate op, so operators can raise supervisor budgets deliberately rather than discovering the limit by losing a run.

## Related
Discovered while completing epic 5e64-d9cd-2dd4-4036 (citric-moudly-vipersquid) after its executor agent died this way. Distinct from bug 08c8-2236-376f-435e (frangible-irongray-adouri), which is a packaging/exit-code defect on the same close path — that one makes a crashed close look successful; this one makes a successful close look hung. They compound: a supervisor that survives the silence may then be told exit 0 by a close that never happened.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A close/review-plan/verify-completion invocation emits at least one progress signal well inside a 600s window, on a repo where the call takes minutes.
- [ ] The documented gate reference states the expected duration range and the interaction with supervisor stall budgets.
data.title: Long-running LLM gate operations emit no incremental output, starving supervising agents' stall watchdogs
